posts.title: Met Office autumn outlook: treat wet and wind as a temporary works load case, not a weather note
posts.excerpt: The Met Office seasonal outlook issued around 11 September 2026 gives a higher-than-normal chance of a warm, wet UK autumn, with windy conditions more likely later in the season as a strong El Nino develops. That is not a forecast for any given Tuesday. It is a prompt for contractors to treat rainfall, reduced ground strength, flooded excavations, saturated platforms and out-of-service crane wind as temporary works load cases now, while there is still time to inspect, drain, re-brief and hold permits. Standard platforms and open-cut trenches do not automatically stay low risk when the ground is wet.
posts.linkedinReady:
A seasonal outlook is not a lift plan and it is not a permit to load.

The Met Office 3-month outlook published this month gives a higher-than-normal chance of a warm, wet UK autumn, with windy conditions more likely later in the season as a strong El Nino develops. That does not tell you what happens on your site this week. It does tell the TWC and TWS to treat rainfall, saturated ground, flooded excavations and out-of-service crane wind as temporary works load cases before the first prolonged wet spell arrives.

HSE excavations guidance remains blunt: support or batter the sides, keep spoil and plant back from the edge, control groundwater and inspect after weather that can change the condition of the excavation. TWf2024:03 is equally clear that a granular working platform is only as good as the formation, drainage and maintenance that keep the design CBR available. CPA TIN 020 still sets a practical UK industry in-service limit of 38 mph (16.5 m/s) for tower cranes so there is time to weather-vane before the OEM out-of-service wind is reached.

Register platforms, excavations, hoardings, scaffolds and crane bases. Reinspect after rainfall. Do not assume last month's dry-weather permit still holds.

body.p: On 11 September 2026 the Met Office restated its latest 3-month outlook: the chance of a warm and wet UK autumn is around one-and-a-half to two times higher than the climatological baseline, with an increased likelihood of windy conditions later in the season. Chief Meteorologist Ian Lisk linked the pattern to a developing El Nino already at near-record strength, while stressing that El Nino is only one driver and does not determine any particular day. BBC Weather and other outlets repeated the same primary Met Office position. This briefing does not treat the outlook as a site forecast. It treats it as a planning signal for temporary works items whose performance changes when the ground is wet and the wind rises.

Wet weather does not invent new temporary works. It changes the load path and the ground that the existing items rely on. Open excavations take water, lose face strength and attract surcharge from plant that can no longer use the planned haul route. Granular working platforms lose CBR when the formation is flooded or the surface is rutted. Hoardings, scaffold sheeting and temporary roofs pick up wind area that may not have been present when the item was first permitted. Tower cranes need time to be placed in the manufacturer's out-of-service condition; the industry in-service limit is not the same number as the design out-of-service wind. Standard does not automatically mean low risk. A shallow trench or a previously competent platform can become high consequence once groundwater, public interface or a crane is added. Provisional category only - to be confirmed by the TWC and the project temporary works procedure.

body.h: Practical TWC and TWS control points
ul: Add a weather-triggered review to the Temporary Works Register for excavations, working platforms, haul roads, hoardings, scaffold interfaces, temporary roofs, crane bases and outrigger pads.

Reinspect excavations after rainfall. Confirm support or batter, edge protection, stand-off of spoil and plant, dewatering and that nobody is working in an unsupported face. HSE excavations guidance is the statutory-duty starting point.

Walk every granular platform against TWf2024:03 principles: formation drainage, surface water run-off, rutting, contamination and whether the design plant still matches what is on site. A wet, rutted platform is a changed design.
Hold or re-issue permit to load / permit to use after exceptional weather. Last week's dry permit does not automatically survive standing water on the mat.
Confirm crane appointed-person limits against CPA TIN 020 (practical UK in-service 38 mph / 16.5 m/s for tower cranes) and the OEM out-of-service configuration, including free slew / weather-vaning.
Check hoarding, sheeted scaffold and temporary roof wind assumptions if the surrounding geometry has changed or if sheeting has been added since the original design.
Do not invent soil parameters or wind speeds. If GI, platform design CBR, plant data or crane charts are missing, stop and request them before recommending a change.
Independent check category remains provisional. Saturated ground, public interface, crane overturning and incomplete drainage normally point to escalation, not a CAT 1 close-out.

Subject to project-specific verification of drawings, loads, ground data, drainage, plant, crane charts, sequence and responsible persons, and to acceptance under the project temporary works procedure. Exact clause references in BS 5975-1:2024, BS EN 1997 and TWf2024:03 are to be confirmed against the project's licensed copy. AI-assisted drafting requires competent review before use on site. posts.title: CIRIA C761 worked example: do not take shear enhancement into the tension side of a piled crane base
posts.excerpt: CROSS-UK Newsletter 82 (3 September 2026) draws attention to Safety Report 1552. A reporter questioned Worked Example 3 in CIRIA C761 Tower crane foundation and tie design: shear enhancement was applied where a piled square crane base is in compression, but the matching shear planes on the tension side under overturning were not checked in the same way. The Expert Panel generally agrees that shear enhancement cannot be used when both the crane leg and the pile are in tension, because no compression strut can form. Crane bases are high-consequence temporary works. Copying a worked example is not a design.
posts.linkedinReady:
A worked example is not a design. CROSS-UK Newsletter 82 (3 September) highlights Safety Report 1552 on CIRIA C761 Worked Example 3 for a square piled tower crane base.

The reporter's concern is simple and high consequence. The example applies shear enhancement on the compression side, where a diagonal strut can form between the crane leg and the pile. Under overturning, the opposite side goes into tension. The Expert Panel generally agrees that shear enhancement cannot be applied when both the crane leg and the pile are in tension, because no compression strut can form. Design for the full shear demand without enhancement, or use a project-specific strut-and-tie model. Do not copy the example into a spreadsheet and call it done.

For the TWC this is a temporary works item with collapse consequence to the public interface. Put the crane base on the Temporary Works Register. Confirm the load cases from the crane supplier, including out-of-service overturning and tension pile reactions. Confirm the check category with the project procedure - high consequence, unusual load path and temporary stability usually mean escalation, not a CAT 1 rubber stamp. Hold permit to load until the design, independent check and as-built pile positions have been reviewed by the competent person.

body.p: CROSS-UK Newsletter 82, issued 3 September 2026, features Safety Report 1552, published 29 June 2026. A reporter reviewed Worked Example 3 in CIRIA C761 Tower crane foundation and tie design, which designs a square piled tower crane base for overturning on both diagonal and orthogonal axes. The example checks beam shear adjacent to the crane leg and adjacent to the pile on the compression side and applies shear enhancement on the basis that part of the force can strut directly into the pile when the load is close to the support. The reporter observed that the corresponding shear planes on the tension side, where overturning puts both the crane leg and the pile reaction into tension, were not checked in the same way. The guide treats tension-side shear as less onerous by inspection. The reporter's own calculations indicated that the tension-side shear capacity adjacent to the pile could be substantially over-utilised if enhancement is stripped out.

A tower crane foundation is a high-consequence temporary works item. Failure of the base is not a local cracking problem; it is overturning of a tall lifting appliance over a live site and often a public interface. CIRIA C761 is authoritative industry guidance, not a project design. The CROSS Expert Panel generally agrees with the reporter's core point: shear enhancement cannot be applied in the worked example when both the crane leg and the pile are in tension, because no compression strut can form between those two locations on the reinforcement detailing shown. A simplified approach is to design the base for the full shear demand without enhancement. That may mean a deeper slab or more reinforcement, but it reduces reliance on intricate detailing that is easy to get wrong on site. Standard does not automatically mean low risk. Provisional category only - to be confirmed by the TWC and the project temporary works procedure. AI outputs and copied examples require competent review before use.

body.h: Practical TWC and TWS control points
ul: Register every tower crane base, piled cap, kentledge arrangement and tie as a temporary works item before the crane is ordered, not after the piles are in the ground.
Treat CIRIA C761 worked examples as illustration only. Require the designer to state, for this geometry and these load cases, whether shear enhancement is being used and on which interfaces.
Demand the crane supplier loads for in-service and out-of-service overturning, including tension pile reactions. Do not accept a single envelope without the sign convention.

Require explicit shear checks on the tension side under overturning. If enhancement is claimed, the designer must demonstrate a compression strut can form. If it cannot, design for full shear without enhancement or use strut-and-tie.
Confirm pile as-built positions against the tolerance assumed in the shear calculation. A pile that has walked is a changed load path.
Independent check category is provisional only and to be confirmed by the TWC. High consequence, public interface and unusual load path normally point to escalation, not a CAT 1 close-out.
Hold permit to load / permit to use until design, check, as-built survey and chocking / holding-down arrangement have been accepted under the project temporary works procedure.

posts.title: Unsupported trench, spoil at the edge: Banstead collapse sentenced at the Old Bailey
posts.excerpt: On 9 September 2026 the Old Bailey sentenced two companies and a contracts manager after Gheorghita Arsene, 33, was buried under about two tonnes of soil in an unsupported trench at Park Road, Banstead on 24 June 2020. HSE and Surrey Police found no trench support and spoil piled immediately next to the edge. A manager had already seen another worker in the same unsupported excavation that day. T Vaughan Limited was fined 650000 pounds plus 40000 costs; Appledorn Developments Limited was fined 500000 pounds. Anthony O'Connor received a 10-month sentence, suspended for 18 months, plus 150 hours unpaid work. Every trench is a temporary works item until the project procedure says otherwise.
